docs.title: pyfossil Official Documentation (v1.0.0)
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for pyfossil, the high-performance Python interface to FOSSIL (FOam diSplacement SImuLator). FOSSIL is a state-of-the-art scientific simulation engine designed for multiphase fluid flow, reactive surfactant transport, and foam displacement in heterogeneous petroleum reservoirs and porous media.

docs.title: 🎯 Simulator Architecture
docs.text:
pyfossil provides the optimal combination of computational speed and modeling flexibility:

  1. C++17 High-Performance Core:
  2. Darcy Flow Discretization: Hybridized Mixed Finite Elements (H-MFE) with Raviart-Thomas (\(RT_0\)) velocity fields and Discontinuous Galerkin (\(DG_0\)) cell-centered pressure fields.
  3. Coupled Stiff Transport: Fully implicit formulation using Jacobian-Free Newton-Krylov (JFNK) integrated with the SUNDIALS CVODE suite (variable-order, variable-step multi-step BDF methods).
  4. Modern Solvers & Preconditioners: Krylov subspace solvers and algebraic multigrid preconditioners from deal.II, PETSc, HYPRE BoomerAMG, PETSc GAMG, and SuiteSparse UMFPACK.

  5. Parallel Acceleration: Multi-threaded shared-memory parallelism using OpenMP.

  6. Python Scripting Usability:

  7. Declarative and intuitive configuration through the unified SimulationData container.
  8. Zero-copy NumPy array interoperability for direct injection of heterogeneous petrophysical maps, initial state distributions, and PVT tables.
  9. Native support for Cartesian structured meshes and 2D/3D unstructured Gmsh grids (.msh).
  10. Dynamic real-time execution hooks (set_step_callback) for intelligent well controllers, physics-informed machine learning, and optimization algorithms.

docs.title: 📚 Documentation Contents
docs.text:
• Installation Guide: Step-by-step instructions for installing the pre-compiled ManyLinux standalone .whl package.
  • Python API Reference: Detailed documentation of all configuration modules, data classes, enums, properties, and simulator methods.
  • Solvers & Numerical Methods: Theoretical and practical guide to selecting Darcy linear solvers, algebraic multigrid preconditioners, and JFNK transport schemes.
  • Tutorials & Benchmarks: Comprehensive walkthroughs of the 7 research benchmarks located in the examples/ directory.
  • Visualization Guide (plotter.py): Automated post-processing, 1D spatial profile extraction, time-series history plots, and 2D/3D PyVista rendering.

docs.title: 💡 Quick Start Example
docs.text:
import pyfossil

# 1. Instantiate the configuration container
sim = pyfossil.SimulationData()

# 2. Configure a 2D Cartesian mesh (40 x 20 cells, 100 m x 50 m)
sim.global_settings.dimension = 2
sim.global_settings.mesh_type = pyfossil.MeshType.ORTHOGONAL_MESH
sim.orthogonal_geometry.n_x = 40
sim.orthogonal_geometry.n_y = 20
sim.orthogonal_geometry.x_final = 100.0
sim.orthogonal_geometry.y_final = 50.0

# 3. Define petrophysical properties
sim.rock_properties.porosity = 0.20
sim.rock_properties.perm_x = 100.0 * 9.86923e-16 # 100 mD in m^2
sim.rock_properties.perm_y = 100.0 * 9.86923e-16

# 4. Configure solvers
sim.execution_control.darcy_linear_solver = pyfossil.DarcyLinearSolver.CG
sim.execution_control.darcy_preconditioner = pyfossil.DarcyPreconditioner.BOOMER_AMG
sim.execution_control.transport_linear_solver = pyfossil.TransportLinearSolver.GMRES
sim.execution_control.transport_preconditioner = pyfossil.TransportPreconditioner.BLOCK_ILU

# 5. Initialize and execute the simulation engine
simulator = pyfossil.FossilSimulator(sim, "./output_quickstart")
simulator.run()

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text:
pyfossil is distributed as a pre-compiled, self-contained ManyLinux Standalone Wheel (.whl).

All high-performance scientific libraries (deal.II, PETSc, HYPRE, SUNDIALS, NLopt, SuiteSparse UMFPACK, OpenBLAS, and TBB) are bundled and linked internally within the package. No C++ compilation, CMake configuration, or manual library installations are required.

docs.title: 💻 System Requirements
docs.text:
• Operating System: Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+, CentOS/RHEL 8+, Fedora 34+, Arch Linux, etc.).
  • Python: Versions 3.8 through 3.12 (64-bit).
  • Core Python Dependencies: numpy (>= 1.20) and matplotlib (>= 3.3).

docs.title: Method 1: Direct Installation from GitHub Releases (Recommended)
docs.text:
You can install the wheel directly from the GitHub Releases page without cloning the repository:

pip install https://github.com/fylype/pyfossil/releases/download/v1.0.0/pyfossil-1.0.0-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_39_x86_64.whl

(Note: Replace cp312 with your Python version tag, e.g., cp310, cp311, or cp312).

docs.title: Method 2: Installing from a Local Wheel File
docs.text:
If you have downloaded the .whl file locally to your machine:

pip install pyfossil-1.0.0-*.whl

docs.title: ✅ Verifying Installation
docs.text:
Open a terminal and verify that pyfossil loads and initializes properly:

python3 -c "import pyfossil; print(f'pyfossil v{pyfossil.__version__} loaded successfully!'); sim = pyfossil.SimulationData(); print('SimulationData initialization OK!')"

Expected output: 

pyfossil v1.0.0 loaded successfully!
SimulationData initialization OK!

docs.title: 🛠️ Virtual Environment Setup (venv / conda)
docs.text:
Using an isolated virtual environment is recommended for your simulation workflows:

# Create a dedicated virtual environment
python3 -m venv ~/envs/fossil_env

# Activate the virtual environment
source ~/envs/fossil_env/bin/activate

# Upgrade pip and install visualization tools
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install numpy matplotlib pyvista pandas

# Install pyfossil
pip install pyfossil-1.0.0-*.whl

docs.title: Post-Processing and Visualization: FossilPlotter Guide
docs.text: plotter.py provides the FossilPlotter class, an automated, publication-quality post-processing and visualization engine designed specifically for FOSSIL simulation data.

docs.title: 1. Overview and Capabilities
docs.text:
FossilPlotter interfaces directly with FOSSIL output directories containing: * Unstructured VTU files (volume_vars_*.vtu): Spatial saturation, pressure, foam texture, and surfactant distributions. * CSV history tables (wells.csv, time_series.csv): Dynamic Bottom-Hole Pressures (BHP), cumulative fluid injection/production, and phase rates.

Key features: * Publication-Quality Styling: Clean white background, crisp axis spines, configurable LaTeX font rendering, and automated legends. * Automated 1D Spatial Profiling: Interpolates field variables along arbitrary 1D lines through 1D, 2D, or 3D meshes at multiple time steps. * Off-Screen 2D/3D Rendering: Uses PyVista for headless 2D and 3D spatial field rendering and screenshot generation. * Standalone Colorbars: Generates isolated, high-resolution horizontal/vertical colorbars suitable for multi-panel publication figures.

docs.title: 2. Installation and Dependencies
docs.text:
The plotting engine requires: 

pip install numpy matplotlib pyvista pandas

Optional: If latex is installed on your operating system, FossilPlotter automatically enables LaTeX typography.

docs.title: 3. Initialization
docs.text:
from plotter import FossilPlotter

plotter = FossilPlotter(
    output_dir="./output_SPE10_3D",
    dim=3,
    style="seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid",
    use_tex=True
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description output_dir str required Path to the directory where simulation VTU and CSV files are saved. dim int 3 Spatial dimension of the domain (1, 2, or 3). style str 'seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid' Matplotlib stylesheet name. use_tex bool True Enables LaTeX font rendering if latex executable is found in PATH.

docs.title: 4.1. Plotting 1D Spatial Profiles (plot_spatial_1d)
docs.text:
Extracts and plots line profiles of any scalar field variable across multiple time steps.

plotter.plot_spatial_1d(
    target_variable="water_saturation",
    time_steps=[10, 50, 100, 200],
    xlabel="Core Length [m]",
    ylabel="Water Saturation [-]",
    save_path="profiles_Sw.png",
    axis=0,                 # 0 = X-axis, 1 = Y-axis, 2 = Z-axis
    y_limits=(0.0, 1.0),
    title="Water Saturation Advance Along Core"
)

docs.title: 4.2. Plotting Time-Series History (plot_history)
docs.text:
Reads CSV logs produced by wells or global integrators and generates multi-curve time-series plots.

plotter.plot_history(
    filename="wells.csv",
    col_x="time_days",
    cols_y=["INJ1_bhp_psi", "P1_bhp_psi"],
    xlabel="Time [days]",
    ylabel="Bottom-Hole Pressure [psi]",
    save_path="bhp_history.png",
    labels=["Injector 1", "Producer 1"],
    title="Well Pressure Responses"
)

docs.title: 4.3. 2D and 3D Mesh Rendering (plot_spatial_mesh)
docs.text:
Renders 2D or 3D scalar fields directly using PyVista off-screen rendering.

plotter.plot_spatial_mesh(
    target_variable="gas_saturation",
    time_step=150,
    save_path="gas_plume_3d.png",
    cmap="jet_r",
    clim=[0.0, 0.8],
    camera_position="iso",      # 'xy', 'xz', 'yz', or 'iso'
    show_edges=False
)

docs.title: 4.4. Standalone Colorbar Export (plot_isolated_colorbar)
docs.text:
Creates a standalone colorbar graphic for external report formatting.

plotter.plot_isolated_colorbar(
    label_name="Dimensionless Foam Texture $n_D$ [-]",
    cmap="viridis",
    vmin=0.0,
    vmax=1.0,
    orientation="horizontal",
    save_path="colorbar_foam_texture.png"
)

docs.title: 5. Complete Example Script
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
from plotter import FossilPlotter

def main():
    # Instantiate plotter pointing to simulation output
    plotter = FossilPlotter(output_dir="./output_case", dim=2)

    # 1. Plot pressure and saturation along core
    plotter.plot_spatial_1d(
        target_variable="water_saturation",
        time_steps=[0, 25, 50, 100],
        xlabel="X Position [m]",
        ylabel="Water Saturation [-]",
        save_path="water_saturation_evolution.png"
    )

    # 2. Render 2D map at final time step
    vtu_files = plotter.get_vtu_files()
    last_step = len(vtu_files) - 1
    plotter.plot_spatial_mesh(
        target_variable="pressure",
        time_step=last_step,
        save_path="pressure_field_final.png",
        cmap="turbo"
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Python API Reference (pyfossil)
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive reference for the classes, data structures, enumerations, and methods exposed by the pyfossil module.

docs.title: 🏗️ 1. Central Configuration Class: SimulationData
docs.text:
The pyfossil.SimulationData object is the unified repository defining all physical, geometric, fluid, rock, well, and numerical solver configurations.

import pyfossil
sim = pyfossil.SimulationData()

docs.title: 1.1 Global Settings (sim.global_settings)
docs.text:
• dimension (int): Spatial dimension of the domain (1, 2, or 3).
  • mesh_type (pyfossil.MeshType):
  • MeshType.ORTHOGONAL_MESH: Structured Cartesian / orthogonal grid.
  • MeshType.UNSTRUCTURED_MESH: Unstructured mesh imported from Gmsh (.msh).

docs.title: 1.2 Orthogonal Geometry (sim.orthogonal_geometry)
docs.text: Used when mesh_type = MeshType.ORTHOGONAL_MESH. - n_x, n_y, n_z (int): Number of cells in X, Y, and Z directions. - x_init, x_final (float): Beginning and end coordinates along the X-axis [m]. - y_init, y_final (float): Beginning and end coordinates along the Y-axis [m]. - z_init, z_final (float): Beginning and end coordinates along the Z-axis [m]. - block_thickness (float): Extrusion thickness of the reservoir (useful for planar 2D models) [m].

docs.title: 1.3 Unstructured Mesh (sim.unstructured_geometry)
docs.text: Used when mesh_type = MeshType.UNSTRUCTURED_MESH. - mesh_filename (str): Absolute or relative path to the Gmsh mesh file (.msh, formats 2.2 or 4.1).

docs.title: 1.4 Fluid Properties (sim.fluid_properties)
docs.text:
• water_viscosity (float): Dynamic water viscosity \(\mu_w\) [Pa·s].
  • water_density (float): Water density \(\rho_w\) [kg/m³].
  • gas_viscosity (float): Dynamic gas viscosity \(\mu_g\) [Pa·s].
  • gas_density (float): Reference gas density \(\rho_g\) [kg/m³].
  • gas_compressibility (bool): Enables compressible gas regime.
  • gas_state_equation (pyfossil.GasStateEquationModel):
  • GasStateEquationModel.IDEAL_GAS: Ideal gas law.
  • GasStateEquationModel.DENSITY_TABLE: Discrete tabular PVT relationship of Pressure vs. Density.
  • table_density_model.density_table (dict[float, float]): Dictionary mapping {Pressure [Pa]: Density [kg/m³]}.
  • gravity (bool): Enables gravitational acceleration and buoyancy terms.
  • gravity_direction (list[float]): Gravitational acceleration vector \([g_x, g_y, g_z]\) [m/s²].

docs.title: 1.5 Rock Petrophysics (sim.rock_properties)
docs.text:
• perm_x, perm_y, perm_z (float): Absolute permeabilities in X, Y, and Z [m²]. (Note: \(1\text{ mD} \approx 9.86923\times 10^{-16}\text{ m}^2\)).
  • porosity (float): Porosity of the porous medium \(\phi \in (0, 1)\).
  • perm_filename (str): External data point cloud file for permeability (e.g., SPE 10 Model 2).
  • por_filename (str): External data point cloud file for porosity.
  • use_material_ids (bool): Enables petrophysical mapping across Gmsh physical region tags.
  • permeability_x_map (dict[int, float]): Material mapping {Material_ID: Perm_X}.
  • porosity_map (dict[int, float]): Material mapping {Material_ID: Porosity}.
  • use_synthetic_field (bool): Generates a spatially correlated log-normal synthetic field using the built-in stochastic generator.
  • synthetic_rock_field.seed: Integer pseudo-random seed.
  • synthetic_rock_field.permeability_avg: Mean permeability [m²].
  • synthetic_rock_field.porosity_avg: Mean porosity.
  • synthetic_rock_field.heterogeneity: Log-normal variance parameter.
  • upscaling: Directional petrophysical upscaling manager:
  • method_x, method_y, method_z (pyfossil.UpscalingMethod): ARITHMETIC, HARMONIC, GEOMETRIC, POWER_LAW.
  • power_law_exponent_x, power_law_exponent_y: Power-law averaging exponent (e.g., 0.33).

docs.title: 1.6 Rock-Fluid Interactions (sim.rock_fluid_interactions)
docs.text:
• swc (float): Connate / irreducible water saturation \(S_{wc}\).
  • sgr (float): Residual gas saturation \(S_{gr}\).
  • sigma_wg (float): Water-gas interfacial tension \(\sigma_{wg}\) [N/m].
  • rel_perm_model (pyfossil.RelativePermeabilityModel):
  • COREY_BROOKS_KR: Standard Corey-Brooks model.
  • KOVSCEK_KR: Cubic Kovscek curves.
  • ASHOORI_KR: Quadratic Ashoori curves.
  • CUSTOM_KR: Custom saturation exponents \(N_w\) and \(N_g\) (custom_rel_perm.nw, ng).
  • cap_pressure_model (pyfossil.CapillaryPressureModel):
  • NONE: Neglect capillary pressure.
  • LEVERETT_J: Leverett J-function scaled by local permeability and porosity.
  • KOVSCEK_CP, ASHOORI_CP: Foam-specific capillary formulations.

docs.title: 1.7 EOR Mechanisms & Foam Models (sim.eor_mechanisms)
docs.text:
• foam_model (pyfossil.FoamModel): NONE, KOVSCEK, ASHOORI.
  • Ashoori Model Parameters (sim.eor_mechanisms.ashoori_model):
  • A: Lamella division bubble generation parameter.
  • sw_critical: Critical water saturation for capillary transition.
  • max_mob_red: Maximum gas mobility reduction factor (\(MRF\)).
  • K_c: Lamella destruction rate constant [s⁻¹].
  • Kovscek Model Parameters (sim.eor_mechanisms.kovscek_model):
  • k01: Lamella generation rate coefficient.
  • k0m1: Lamella coalescence rate coefficient.
  • refSurf: Reference critical surfactant concentration [wt%].
  • alpha: Bretherton shear-thinning exponent.
  • pcStarMax: Limiting capillary pressure for lamella rupture [Pa].

docs.title: 1.8 Peaceman Well System (sim.wells)
docs.text: Dictionary of wells indexed by identifier string (sim.wells["WellName"]): - well_type (pyfossil.WellType): INJECTOR or PRODUCER. - well_control (pyfossil.WellControl): - WellControl.FLOW_RATE: Target volumetric flow rate [m³/s]. - WellControl.BHP: Bottom-Hole Pressure constraint [Pa]. - well_value (float or dict): Operational constraint value (supports piecewise schedules {time: value}). - well_radius (float): Wellbore radius \(r_w\) [m]. - skin_factor (float): Dimensionless well skin factor. - include_hydrostatic_head (bool): Accounts for hydrostatic fluid head variation along well perforations. - trajectory_coords (list[float]): 3D well trajectory coordinates [x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2] from heel to toe.

docs.title: 1.9 Initial and Boundary Conditions (sim.initial_and_boundary_conditions)
docs.text:
• initial_state:
  • pressure_init.constant_value: Initial reservoir pressure [Pa].
  • initialization[pyfossil.Variable.SW].constant_value: Initial water saturation \(S_w \in [0, 1]\).
  • initialization[pyfossil.Variable.CS].constant_value: Initial surfactant concentration \(C_s\) [wt%].
  • Cartesian Mesh Boundaries: Predefined faces "Left", "Right", "Top", "Bottom", "Front", "Back".
  • Unstructured Mesh Boundaries: Defined dynamically via setup_dynamic_boundaries(["Name1", "Name2", ...]).
  • Boundary Properties:
  • darcy_boundary_type: DIRICHLET (prescribed pressure) or NEUMANN (prescribed Darcy flux [m/s]).
  • darcy_boundary_value: Scalar value or time schedule {t0: v0, t1: v1}.
  • trans_boundary_type: DIRICHLET, INFLOW_DIRICHLET, INFLOW_NEUMANN_FW, OUTFLOW, NO_FLOW.
  • trans_boundary_values[pyfossil.Variable.*]: Prescribed injected volume fraction or concentration.

docs.title: 1.10 Numerical Solvers & Execution Control (sim.execution_control)
docs.text:
• variables (set[pyfossil.Variable]): Set of active conservation equations:
  • Variable.SW: Water saturation.
  • Variable.ND: Foam bubble texture density.
  • Variable.CS: Surfactant concentration.
  • darcy_linear_solver (pyfossil.DarcyLinearSolver):
  • CG: Conjugate Gradient (ideal for symmetric positive-definite condensed systems).
  • MINRES: Minimal Residual (optimal for pure-Neumann problems with nullspace closure).
  • GMRES, BiCGSTAB: General Krylov solvers for nonsymmetric matrices.
  • UMFPACK: Direct sparse LU factorization (exact and robust for 1D/2D).
  • darcy_preconditioner (pyfossil.DarcyPreconditioner):
  • BOOMER_AMG: HYPRE BoomerAMG algebraic multigrid (peak performance on large 3D meshes).
  • GAMG: PETSc native Geometric-Algebraic Multigrid.
  • ICC: Incomplete Cholesky Factorization.
  • PARASAILS: Parallel Sparse Approximate Inverse.
  • NONE: Unpreconditioned iterative solver.
  • transport_linear_solver (pyfossil.TransportLinearSolver):
  • GMRES, BICGSTAB, TFQMR: Native SUNDIALS Krylov solvers tightly coupled to JFNK.
  • GMRES_PETSC, BCGSL_PETSC, BICGSTAB_PETSC: PETSc KSP solvers coupled to JFNK.
  • transport_preconditioner (pyfossil.TransportPreconditioner):
  • BLOCK_ILU: Block-Jacobi incomplete LU per cell (default, excellent efficiency).
  • GLOBAL_ILU: Global coupled ILU across the full mesh.
  • BOOMER_AMG: Algebraic multigrid for transport systems.
  • NONE: Pure matrix-free JFNK without preconditioning.
  • darcy_time_step_strategy (pyfossil.DarcyTimeStepStrategy):
  • NONE: Fixed constant Darcy macro time step.
  • SW_VARIATION: Adaptive time stepping governed by maximum saturation variation \(\Delta S_w\).
  • PAZ_VELOCITY: Adaptive time stepping based on velocity \(L_2\) norm variation (Paz et al., 2021).
  • num_method (pyfossil.NumericalMethod):
  • KNP: Central-Upwind scheme of Kurganov, Noelle & Petrova (2001).
  • KPP: Central-Upwind scheme of Kurganov, Petrova & Popova (2007) for non-convex fractional flows.
  • abstol, reltol (float): Absolute and relative tolerances for CVODE integration.
  • num_threads (int): Number of OpenMP parallel execution threads.

docs.title: 🎮 2. Executive Engine: FossilSimulator
docs.text: Manages grid assembly, physical field mapping, the coupled Darcy-transport time-stepping loop, and output generation.

docs.title: 2.1 Constructor and Core Methods
docs.text:
simulator = pyfossil.FossilSimulator(sim_data, output_dir="./output")
- run(): Executes the complete simulation from initial state to final_time. - set_step_callback(callback_fn): Registers a Python callback invoked after each macro time step. - Callback signature: callback(t_physical: float, sim, sim_data) -> bool - Returning True continues simulation; returning False triggers graceful early termination. - get_current_well_bhp(well_name: str) -> float: Returns the current Bottom-Hole Pressure of the specified well in Pascals. - get_current_well_rate(well_name: str) -> float: Returns the current volumetric flow rate of the specified well in m³/s. - set_well_bhp(well_name: str, bhp_pa: float): Dynamically modifies the target BHP of a well during execution. - set_well_rate(well_name: str, rate_m3_s: float): Dynamically modifies the target flow rate of a well during execution.

docs.title: Solvers & Numerical Methods Guide
docs.text: FOSSIL employs a high-order fractional-step (operator-splitting) scheme coupling Darcy hydrodynamics (pressure and velocity) with nonlinear multiphase transport (phase saturations and chemical species).

docs.title: 🌊 1. Darcy Flow: Hybridized Mixed Finite Elements (H-MFE)
docs.text:
The spatial discretization utilizes Raviart-Thomas (\(RT_0\)) vector elements for velocity and Discontinuous Galerkin (\(DG_0\)) scalar elements for cell-centered pressure.

Through elemental static condensation (Schur complement reduction), local cell velocities and cell pressures are eliminated analytically at the element level, reducing the indefinite saddle-point system to a sparse global linear system formulated strictly for trace pressures on inter-element faces:

\[H \boldsymbol{\Lambda} = \mathbf{R}\]

docs.title: 1.1 Mathematical Properties of the Darcy Matrix \(H\):
docs.text:
• Symmetric Positive-Definite (SPD): Occurs when at least one Dirichlet pressure boundary condition is prescribed or at least one well operates under Bottom-Hole Pressure (BHP) control.
  • Symmetric Positive Semi-Definite (SPSD with Constant Nullspace): Occurs when all domain boundaries are prescribed Darcy fluxes (pure Neumann) and all wells operate under rate control. FOSSIL automatically projects out the constant null eigenvector (\(\mathbf{1}\)), guaranteeing mathematical closure and unconditional iterative convergence.

docs.title: 1.2 Darcy Linear Solvers Catalog:
docs.text: Solver Mathematical Property Complexity Practical Recommendation CG (Conjugate Gradient) Symmetric positive-definite Optimal (\(O(N)\) with AMG) Recommended for the majority of 2D and 3D reservoirs. MINRES (Minimal Residual) Symmetric and indefinite/singular \(O(N)\) Recommended for pure Neumann problems without BHP wells. BiCGSTAB Nonsymmetric or slightly indefinite Robust Excellent alternative for unstructured meshes with distorted elements. GMRES General asymmetric systems Memory scales with restart size Ideal for severe petrophysical anisotropy. UMFPACK Direct sparse \(LU\) factorization Exact, \(O(N^{1.5})\) to \(O(N^2)\) Recommended for 1D and moderate 2D meshes. Eliminates iterative convergence tuning.

docs.title: 1.3 Darcy Preconditioners:
docs.text: Preconditioner Library Mechanism Recommended Use Case BOOMER_AMG HYPRE / PETSc Classical Algebraic Multigrid with parallel coarsening Gold standard for large-scale 3D field models. GAMG PETSc Native Geometric-Algebraic Multigrid High performance without external HYPRE dependency. ICC deal.II / PETSc Incomplete Cholesky Factorization (\(IC(0)\)) Structured 2D grids. PARASAILS HYPRE / PETSc Parallel Sparse Approximate Inverse Reservoirs where anisotropy degrades AMG coarsening. NONE - No preconditioning Used with direct UMFPACK or MINRES.

docs.title: 🚀 2. Implicit Multiphase Transport: JFNK Formulation
docs.text: The hyperbolic conservation laws governing water saturation (\(S_w\)), foam texture (\(n_D\)), and surfactant (\(C_s\)) exhibit strong flux nonlinearities and stiff kinetics requiring implicit multi-step time integration (SUNDIALS CVODE BDF).

docs.title: 2.1 What is JFNK (Jacobian-Free Newton-Krylov)?
docs.text:
In traditional matrix-based implicit methods, each Newton iteration requires assembling, allocating, and storing a massive coupled Jacobian matrix, consuming hundreds of gigabytes of RAM on fine 3D grids.

In JFNK, the Krylov subspace solver (GMRES or BiCGStab) never forms the Jacobian matrix explicitly. Instead, it evaluates the action of the Jacobian on a search direction \(\mathbf{v}\) via a finite-difference directional derivative:

\[J(\mathbf{u}) \mathbf{v} \approx \frac{F(\mathbf{u} + \epsilon \mathbf{v}) - F(\mathbf{u})}{\epsilon}\]

where \(\epsilon\) is an optimal perturbation parameter computed dynamically from integrator error tolerances.

docs.title: 2.2 Preconditioning in JFNK
docs.text:
To accelerate Krylov convergence while maintaining the memory advantages of matrix-free evaluation, FOSSIL implements right preconditioning:

\[[J P^{-1}] (P \mathbf{v}) = -F(\mathbf{u})\]

where \(P\) is a sparse coupling matrix: - BLOCK_ILU (Default & Recommended): Inverts local block matrices coupling the conservation variables within each single cell (e.g., \(S_w, n_D, C_s\)). Negligible memory footprint and excellent convergence acceleration. - GLOBAL_ILU: Couples inter-element advective fluxes across the full mesh; ideal for large CFL numbers. - BOOMER_AMG: Applies algebraic multigrid preconditioning to the transport system. - NONE: Pure matrix-free Krylov iteration without preconditioning (ideal for small time steps).

docs.title: Tutorials & Benchmarks Guide
docs.text: The examples/ directory in the repository provides 7 ready-to-run simulation setups. Each tutorial includes a fully commented Python driver script, required mesh files (.msh, .geo), input data arrays (.dat), post-processing visualization scripts (plot.py), and a dedicated README.md.

docs.title: 📋 Benchmark Catalog
docs.text: Tutorial Directory Domain & Dimension Physical Phenomena Linear Solvers & Preconditioners 01 01_ashoori_coreflood_1d 1D / 200 cells Ashoori et al. (2011) experimental coreflood; bubble generation, coalescing transition, and mobility reduction. UMFPACK + JFNK GMRES 02 02_unstructured_2d_materials 2D Unstructured Gmsh with well cavity Multi-region petrophysical mapping (4 Material IDs), Kovscek Local Equilibrium foam, surfactant transport, real-gas PVT density table. BiCGSTAB + BoomerAMG 03 03_unstructured_3d_hole 3D Tetrahedral Gmsh with well cavity Radial injection from perforation cavity, 3D spatially correlated log-normal rock field, 7 dynamic boundary faces. docs.title: 🏃 Running the Tutorials
docs.text:
Navigate to any tutorial folder and execute the Python driver script:

cd examples/01_ashoori_coreflood_1d
python run_ashoori2011.py

# Generate publication-quality comparison plots:
python plot.py

For 2D and 3D simulation cases (such as 02, 03, 04, and 07), output directories contain standard VTU files (volume_vars_*.vtu) that can be opened directly in ParaView or visualized off-screen using FossilPlotter.
